beats.text: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, by Lewis Carroll.
Chapter One. Down the Rabbit-Hole.
Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank, and of having nothing to do.
There was nothing so very remarkable in that; nor did Alice think it so very much out of the way to hear the Rabbit say to itself.
Oh dear! Oh dear! I shall be late!
But when the Rabbit actually took a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket, and looked at it, and then hurried on, Alice started to her feet.
In another moment down went Alice after it.
Well!
Thought Alice to herself.
After such a fall as this, I shall think nothing of tumbling down stairs!
What a curious feeling!
Said Alice.
I must be shutting up like a telescope.
Soon her eye fell on a little glass box that was lying under the table.
She opened it, and found in it a very small cake, on which the words "Eat me" were beautifully marked in currants.
Well, I'll eat it.
Said Alice.
And if it makes me grow larger, I can reach the key; and if it makes me grow smaller, I can creep under the door.
She ate a little bit, and said anxiously to herself.
Which way? Which way?
So she set to work, and very soon finished off the cake.

characters.name: Narrator
characters.description: A warm, measured English reading voice with a gently whimsical lilt, well suited to a Victorian children's fantasy.

characters.name: The White Rabbit
characters.description: A fussy, high-pitched, slightly nasal English voice in a perpetual flustered hurry, prone to anxious exclamations.

characters.name: Alice
characters.description: A bright, curious young English girl with a clear, light voice that swings easily between wonder, earnestness, and playful self-assurance.
